messages:
eli: FYI: Finance + Growth approved three small billing policy updates. Posting here before customer comms. :loudspeaker:

rachel: what are the changes?

eli: TL;DR:
1) Introduce a $10/month minimum invoice floor for free and trial accounts that exceed API usage thresholds (aim: reduce microbilling churn).
2) Free-tier rate limits tightened: free accounts move from 60 rps -> 20 rps, and token cap per minute lowered. Paid tiers unchanged.
3) Billing periods: for self-serve Hosted accounts we will align invoice period to account-creation anchor (customer's billing day = account creation day) instead of calendar month; reserved contracts unchanged.

billing-bot: Note: Min-invoice applies only when monthly usage > $0 and < $10; we issue a single $10 invoice instead of $X < $10. Existing paid accounts unaffected.

tom: will we prorate that on first/last month?

eli: First month is prorated by usage; min-floor only applies after prorate calculation. Finance provided examples and a matrix.

support: console UX? customers will see unexpected $10 invoices if they use tiny amounts.

rachel: CS will add a banner and email template. We'll include examples and opt-out info for partners.

billing-bot: Rate-limit change enforced via gateway config: `free_tier_rps=20`. Token caps documented in billing FAQ.

tom: accounting impact?

billing-bot: Finance: revenue recognition unaffected; min-invoice charged as normal revenue for the service period. Forecast model updated.

eli: Customer comms schedule: internal notice today, customer emails 14 days before effective date, console banner 7 days before. Docs + FAQ updated by rachel.

support: action items copied to #support-playbooks. I'll draft the CS script and email.

eli: Owners:
- Docs/FAQ: rachel
- Billing infra rollout: tom
- CS emails & scripts: support
- Finance review: finance team

billing-bot: Task created: `min-invoice-free-tier-2026-11` assigned to tom, rachel, support. Reminder set for 14 days pre-rollout.

eli: thanks all. Please escalate any edge cases to me or ping finance. :thumbsup:
